questions.questionText: P, Q and R can finish a work in 5 days, 10 days, and 15 days, respectively, working alone. P and Q works on first day, P and R works on second day and P and Q works on third day and so on till the work is completed. In how many days the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(5, 10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of R} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (P + Q)} = 6 + 3 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (P + R)} = 6 + 2 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 9 + 8 = 17\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work after 2 days} = 30 - 17 = 13\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 3 (P + Q)} = 9\text{ units. Remaining} = 13 - 9 = 4\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 4 (P + R)} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 2 + 1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A, B and C can complete a piece of work separately in 10, 20 and 40 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be completed if A is assisted by both B and C every third day?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 20, 40) = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 1$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 2 (A)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 3 (A + B + C)} = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 4 + 4 + 7 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 2 cycles (6 days), work done} = 2 \times 15 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 40 - 30 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 7: A does } 4\text{ units. Remaining} = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 8: A does } 4\text{ units. Remaining} = 2\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 9: (A + B + C) take } \frac{2}{7}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + 2 + \frac{2}{7} = 8\frac{2}{7}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: Ruchi, Khushi and Teju can do a piece of work in 30, 40 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can Ruchi do the work, if she is assisted by both Khushi and Teju on every third day?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 40, 60) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Ruchi} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Khushi} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of Teju} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (Ruchi)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 2 (Ruchi)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 3 (All three)} = 9$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 4 + 4 + 9 = 17\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 7 cycles (21 days), work done} = 7 \times 17 = 119\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 119 = 1\text{ unit}$$
$$\text{Day 22: Ruchi takes } \frac{1}{4}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 21 + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{85}{4}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days respectively. If B works daily and is supported by A and C on alternate days beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(11, 20, 55) = 220\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 20,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 11,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 4$$
$$\text{Day 1 (B + A)} = 11 + 20 = 31\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (B + C)} = 11 + 4 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 31 + 15 = 46\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 4 cycles (8 days), work done} = 4 \times 46 = 184\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 220 - 184 = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 9 (B + A)} = 31\text{ units. Remaining} = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 10 (B + C)} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 8 + 1 + \frac{1}{3} = 9\frac{1}{3}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText:
A alone can do a work in 11 days. B alone can do the same work in 22 days. C alone can do the same work in 33 days. They work in the following manner:
Day 1: A and B work.
Day 2: B and C work.
Day 3: C and A work.
Day 4: A and B work.
In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(11, 22, 33) = 66\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A + B)} = 6 + 3 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (B + C)} = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 3 (C + A)} = 2 + 6 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 9 + 5 + 8 = 22\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{66}{22} = 3\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A and B complete a work in 24 and 30 days, respectively, working 10 hours per day. The work is to be done in two shifts. The morning shift is for 6 hours and the evening shift is for 4 hours. On the first day, A works in the morning and B works in the evening, and they interchange their shifts every day. On which day did the work get completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(240, 300) = 1200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Hourly efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Hourly efficiency of B} = 4$$
$$\text{Odd days (A in morning 6h, B in evening 4h)} = (6 \times 5) + (4 \times 4) = 46\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Even days (B in morning 6h, A in evening 4h)} = (6 \times 4) + (4 \times 5) = 44\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 46 + 44 = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 13 cycles (26 days), work done} = 13 \times 90 = 1170\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 1200 - 1170 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{On Day 27 (morning shift), A works 6h and does } 6 \times 5 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work is completed on the 27th day.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively, R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day. In how many days is the work finished?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 15, 10) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of S} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of T} = 6$$
$$\text{Day 1 (R + T)} = 3 + 6 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (R + S)} = 3 + 4 = 7\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 9 + 7 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 3 cycles (6 days), work done} = 3 \times 16 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 48 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 7 (R + T)} = 9\text{ units. Remaining} = 3\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 8 (R + S)} = \frac{3}{7}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + 1 + \frac{3}{7} = \frac{52}{7}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A and B are equally efficient, and each can individually complete a piece of work in 36 days, if none takes any holiday. A and B started working together on this piece of work, but A took a day off after every five days of work, while B took a day off after every seven days of work. If they had started work on 1 July 2021, on which date was the work completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let efficiency of each be } 1\text{ unit/day. Total work} = 36\text{ units.}$$
$$\text{A rests on days: 6, 12, 18, 24...}$$
$$\text{B rests on days: 8, 16, 24...}$$
$$\text{Daily work tracking:}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 5: both work } \implies 5 \times 2 = 10\text{ units (cum. 10)}$$
$$\text{Day 6: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 11)}$$
$$\text{Day 7: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 13)}$$
$$\text{Day 8: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 14)}$$
$$\text{Days 9 to 11: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 20)}$$
$$\text{Day 12: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 21)}$$
$$\text{Days 13 to 15: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 27)}$$
$$\text{Day 16: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 28)}$$
$$\text{Day 17: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 30)}$$
$$\text{Day 18: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 31)}$$
$$\text{Days 19 and 20: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 35)}$$
$$\text{Day 21: both work, needing only } 1\text{ unit to reach 36 units.}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work is completed on Day 21, i.e., 21 July 2021.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A and B are equally efficient, and each could individually complete a piece of work in 30 days, if none took any holiday. A and B started working together on this piece of work, but A took a day off after every four days of work, while B took a day off after every five days of work. If the duo had started work on 01 August 2022, on which date was the work completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let efficiency of each be } 1\text{ unit/day. Total work} = 30\text{ units.}$$
$$\text{A rests on days: 5, 10, 15, 20...}$$
$$\text{B rests on days: 6, 12, 18, 24...}$$
$$\text{Daily tracking:}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 4: both work } \implies 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ units (cum. 8)}$$
$$\text{Day 5: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 9)}$$
$$\text{Day 6: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 10)}$$
$$\text{Days 7 to 9: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 16)}$$
$$\text{Day 10: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 17)}$$
$$\text{Day 11: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 19)}$$
$$\text{Day 12: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 20)}$$
$$\text{Days 13 to 14: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 24)}$$
$$\text{Day 15: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 25)}$$
$$\text{Days 16 to 17: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 29)}$$
$$\text{Day 18: A works (B rests), doing the 30th unit.}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work was completed on Day 18, i.e., 18 August 2022.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: Two men A and B, each working alone by working 12 hours per day, can complete a work in 20 days. For execution of the work, it was decided that A and B would be working for 8 and 6 hours per day, respectively, on alternate days starting with A. If it takes x days and y hours to complete the work then (x, y) is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 12 = 240\text{ man-hours}$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A): } 8\text{ hours},\quad \text{Day 2 (B): } 6\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 8 + 6 = 14\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{In 17 cycles (34 days), work done} = 17 \times 14 = 238\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 240 - 238 = 2\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{On Day 35, A works for 2 hours to complete the remaining work.}$$
$$\text{Hence, } x = 34\text{ full days and } y = 2\text{ hours} \implies (x, y) = (34, 2)$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: Ratnesh and Vineet worked on alternate days, starting with Ratnesh. The entire work got completed in $54\frac{3}{4}$ days. If Ratnesh alone can finish the work in 48 days, then in how many days can Vineet alone do the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total time} = 54\frac{3}{4}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Starting with Ratnesh: Ratnesh worked on odd days (27 full days } + \frac{3}{4}\text{ day}) = \frac{111}{4}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Vineet worked on even days (27 full days)}$$
$$\text{Daily rate of Ratnesh} = \frac{1}{48}$$
$$\text{Work done by Ratnesh} = \frac{111}{4} \times \frac{1}{48} = \frac{37}{64}$$
$$\text{Work done by Vineet} = 1 - \frac{37}{64} = \frac{27}{64}$$
$$\text{Daily rate of Vineet} = \frac{27/64}{27} = \frac{1}{64}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Vineet alone} = 64\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A man and woman working on alternate days can finish a work in 15 days if the man works on the first day. The same work is finished in 14.5 days if they work on alternate days and if the woman starts on the first day. The work will be finished by a man alone in ______ days.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Case 1 (Man starts, 15 days): Man works 8 days, Woman works 7 days: } W = 8M + 7W$$
$$\text{Case 2 (Woman starts, 14.5 days): Woman works 7.5 days, Man works 7 days: } W = 7M + 7.5W$$
$$8M + 7W = 7M + 7.5W \implies M = 0.5W \implies W = 2M$$
$$\text{Total work } W = 8M + 7(2M) = 22M$$
$$\text{Time taken by a man alone} = 22\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: To do a certain work, Ajay and Bharat work on alternate days, with Bharat starting the work on the first day. Ajay can finish the work alone in 32 days. If the work gets completed in exactly 8 days, then Bharat alone can finish 7 times the same work in _____ days.
questions.solution:
$$\text{In 8 days with Bharat starting, Bharat works 4 days and Ajay works 4 days.}$$
$$\text{Work done by Ajay in 4 days} = \frac{4}{32} = \frac{1}{8}$$
$$\text{Work done by Bharat in 4 days} = 1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$$
$$\text{Rate of Bharat} = \frac{7/8}{4} = \frac{7}{32}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time for Bharat to complete 7 times the work} = \frac{7}{7/32} = 32\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: To do a certain work, A and B work on alternate days with B beginning the work on the first day. A alone can complete the same work in 24 days. If the work gets completed in $11\frac{1}{3}$ days, then B alone can complete $\frac{7}{9}$ part of the original work in:
questions.solution:
$$\text{In } 11\frac{1}{3}\text{ days with B starting:}$$
$$\text{B works on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 (6 full days)}$$
$$\text{A works on days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (5 days) } + \frac{1}{3}\text{ of day 12} = \frac{16}{3}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by A} = \frac{16}{3} \times \frac{1}{24} = \frac{2}{9}$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 6 days} = 1 - \frac{2}{9} = \frac{7}{9}$$
$$\text{Hence, B alone completes } \frac{7}{9}\text{ of the original work in } 6\text{ days.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: Aman and Rajan are working at a construction site. In some engineering experiment, Aman is constructing a wall, while Rajan is demolishing that wall. Aman can completely build the wall in 15 days, while Rajan will take 20 days to completely demolish the wall. In how many days will the complete wall be built for the first time if they work on alternate days, with Aman working on the 1st day?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Aman (building)} = +4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Rajan (demolishing)} = -3\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Net work in 2-day cycle} = +4 - 3 = +1\text{ unit}$$
$$\text{Target before final building day} = 60 - 4 = 56\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days to reach 56 units} = 56 \times 2 = 112\text{ days}$$
$$\text{On Day 113, Aman builds 4 units: total reaches } 56 + 4 = 60\text{ units (completely built).}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 113\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questions.questionText: A can do a piece of work in 36 days, while B can do it in 48 days. B worked on it for 12 days and leaves it. How many days will A take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 48) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 12 days} = 12 \times 3 = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 144 - 36 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{108}{4} = 27\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. They work together for 2 days and then A leaves. How long will B take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 2 days} = 2 \times (3 + 2) = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: P and Q can do a work together in 30 days. Q and R can do the same work together in 24 days and R and P together in 20 days. They started the work together, but Q and R left after 10 days. How many more days will P take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 24, 20) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Eff}(P + Q) = 4,\quad \text{Eff}(Q + R) = 5,\quad \text{Eff}(R + P) = 6$$
$$2 \times \text{Eff}(P + Q + R) = 15 \implies \text{Eff}(P + Q + R) = 7.5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 7.5 - 5 = 2.5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by all three in 10 days} = 10 \times 7.5 = 75\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 75 = 45\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P alone} = \frac{45}{2.5} = 18\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: Rohan alone can complete a work in 12 days and Hari alone can complete it in 16 days. They both work for 3 days and then Rohan leaves the work. After that Hari works alone and completes the work. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 16) = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Rohan} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Hari} = 3$$
$$\text{Work done by both in 3 days} = 3 \times (4 + 3) = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 48 - 21 = 27\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Hari alone} = \frac{27}{3} = 9\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for work completion} = 3 + 9 = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: P can do a piece of work in 30 days and Q in 40 days. They work together for 4 days and then Q leaves. The number of days taken by P to finish the remaining work is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 40) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = 3$$
$$\text{Work done by (P + Q) in 4 days} = 4 \times (4 + 3) = 28\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 28 = 92\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P alone} = \frac{92}{4} = 23\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A and B can do a work in 15 days and 30 days, respectively. They start working together, but A leaves after 3 days. How much time will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(15, 30) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 3 days} = 3 \times (2 + 1) = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 30 - 9 = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{21}{1} = 21\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: Raja and Rocky together can complete painting work in 5 days. Together they both start painting, but after 2 days, Rocky falls sick and leaves the work. If Raja completes the remaining painting in 4 days, find the number of days in which Rocky alone can do the work.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Work done by (Raja + Rocky) in 2 days} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 1 - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5}$$
$$\text{Rate of Raja} = \frac{3/5}{4} = \frac{3}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Combined rate} = \frac{1}{5} = \frac{4}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Rate of Rocky} = \frac{4}{20} - \frac{3}{20} = \frac{1}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Rocky alone} = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A and B can complete a work in 36 days and 45 days respectively. They worked together for 2 days and then A left the work. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 45) = 180\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 4$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 2 days} = 2 \times (5 + 4) = 18\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 180 - 18 = 162\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{162}{4} = 40.5\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: X can complete half of the work in 20 days and Y can do one-fifth of the same work in 10 days. X started the work and left after 8 days. Then Y took over to complete the remaining work. The total number of days taken by them to complete the work is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time for X to complete whole work} = 20 \times 2 = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for Y to complete whole work} = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(40, 50) = 200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of X} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of Y} = 4$$
$$\text{Work done by X in 8 days} = 8 \times 5 = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 200 - 40 = 160\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Y alone} = \frac{160}{4} = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days taken by them} = 8 + 40 = 48\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: B and C can complete a work alone in 10 days and 30 days respectively. They began the work together but B left the work after some days and C completed the remaining work in 10 days. After how many days from the beginning B left the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 30) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by C alone in last 10 days} = 10 \times 1 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work done by (B + C)} = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of B and C} = 3 + 1 = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days B and C worked together} = \frac{20}{4} = 5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Hence, B left after 5 days from the beginning.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A can complete work in 25 days and B can complete the same work in 20 days. They started the work together but B left after 4 days and A continued to work. In how many days will the entire work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(25, 20) = 100\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 5$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 4 days} = 4 \times (4 + 5) = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100 - 36 = 64\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{64}{4} = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete entire work} = 4 + 16 = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A, B and C can individually complete a work in 24, 15 and 12 days respectively. B and C started the work and left after working for 3 days, how many days will A take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 15, 12) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 8,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 10$$
$$\text{Work done by (B + C) in 3 days} = 3 \times (8 + 10) = 54\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 54 = 66\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{66}{5} = 13\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: Shivam can do a piece of work in 6 days and Vivek in 24 days. They started work together but Shivam left the work 3 days before its completion. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(6, 24) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Shivam} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Vivek} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by Vivek alone in last 3 days} = 3 \times 1 = 3\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done together by Shivam and Vivek} = 24 - 3 = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days worked together} = \frac{21}{4 + 1} = \frac{21}{5} = 4\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete the work} = 4\frac{1}{5} + 3 = 7\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A and B can individually complete a piece of work in 18 days and 30 days, respectively. A and B started working together, but A left $16\frac{2}{3}$ days before the work is completed and B alone completed the rest of the work. For how many days did A work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 30) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3$$
$$16\frac{2}{3}\text{ days} = \frac{50}{3}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by B alone in the last } \frac{50}{3}\text{ days} = \frac{50}{3} \times 3 = 50\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work done by (A + B) together} = 90 - 50 = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of (A + B)} = 5 + 3 = 8\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days A and B worked together} = \frac{40}{8} = 5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Therefore, A worked for 5 days.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: P, Q and R, when working individually, can complete a job in, respectively, 36 days, 48 days and 144 days. P, Q and R start working together. P leaves the job 12 days before completion and Q leaves the job 8 days before completion. R works from the beginning till the end of the job. Determine the total number of days taken to complete the job.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 48, 144) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{144}{36} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{144}{48} = 3$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{144}{144} = 1$$
$$\text{Let the total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$4(T - 12) + 3(T - 8) + 1(T) = 144$$
$$4T - 48 + 3T - 24 + T = 144$$
$$8T - 72 = 144 \implies 8T = 216 \implies T = 27\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: Benny can do a piece of work in 24 days. Chetan and David can do the same work individually in 36 and 48 days respectively. All of them begin the work together. However, Benny leaves the work 4 days before the completion of work and Chetan leaves the work 10 days before the completion of the work. David worked till the end and completed the work. Find the number of days in which the work was completed.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 36, 48) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Benny} = \frac{144}{24} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Chetan} = \frac{144}{36} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of David} = \frac{144}{48} = 3$$
$$\text{Let total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$6(T - 4) + 4(T - 10) + 3T = 144$$
$$6T - 24 + 4T - 40 + 3T = 144$$
$$13T - 64 = 144 \implies 13T = 208 \implies T = 16\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: P, Q and R can complete a work alone in 12, 15 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together. P left the work 8 days before the work was completed and Q left the work 5 days after P had left. R completed the remaining work alone. How many days will be required to complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{60}{12} = 5$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{60}{15} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{60}{20} = 3$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days. P left } 8 \text{ days before completion, so P worked for } (T - 8) \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Q left } 5 \text{ days after P, so Q worked for } (T - 8 + 5) = (T - 3) \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{R worked for all } T \text{ days.}$$
$$5(T - 8) + 4(T - 3) + 3T = 60$$
$$5T - 40 + 4T - 12 + 3T = 60$$
$$12T - 52 = 60 \implies 12T = 112 \implies T = \frac{112}{12} = \frac{28}{3}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: Aarif, Arun and Abraham can do a work in 12, 20 and 24 days, respectively. They all begin together. Aarif leaves the work 1 day, Arun 3 days and Abraham 4 days before its completion. In how many days is the work finished?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 20, 24) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Aarif} = \frac{120}{12} = 10$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Arun} = \frac{120}{20} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Abraham} = \frac{120}{24} = 5$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$10(T - 1) + 6(T - 3) + 5(T - 4) = 120$$
$$10T - 10 + 6T - 18 + 5T - 20 = 120$$
$$21T - 48 = 120 \implies 21T = 168 \implies T = 8\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A alone can do a work in 14 days. B alone can do the same work in 28 days. C alone can do the same work in 56 days. They started working together and completed the work such that B was not working on last 2 days and A did not work in last 3 days. In how many days (total) was the work completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(14, 28, 56) = 56\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{56}{14} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{56}{28} = 2$$
$$\text{Efficiency of C} = \frac{56}{56} = 1$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{A worked for } (T - 3) \text{ days, B worked for } (T - 2) \text{ days, and C worked for } T \text{ days.}$$
$$4(T - 3) + 2(T - 2) + 1(T) = 56$$
$$4T - 12 + 2T - 4 + T = 56$$
$$7T - 16 = 56 \implies 7T = 72 \implies T = \frac{72}{7}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A, B and C separately can do a piece of work in 18, 36 and 54 days respectively. They started the work together, but B and C left 5 days and 10 days respectively before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 36, 54) = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{108}{18} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{108}{36} = 3$$
$$\text{Efficiency of C} = \frac{108}{54} = 2$$
$$\text{Let total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$6T + 3(T - 5) + 2(T - 10) = 108$$
$$6T + 3T - 15 + 2T - 20 = 108$$
$$11T - 35 = 108 \implies 11T = 143 \implies T = 13\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questions.questionText: A can do $\frac{1}{5}$ of a piece of work in 20 days, B can do 30% of the same work in 36 days, while C can do 80% of the same work in 160 days. B and C together started and worked for x days. After x days B left the work, and A joined C and both completed the remaining work in $(x - 41)$ days. If the ratio between the work done by $(B + C)$ together to the work done by $(A + C)$ together is $19 : 6$, then what fraction of the same work can be completed by C alone in 2x days?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total days for A} = 20 \times 5 = 100\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for B} = 36 \times \frac{10}{3} = 120\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for C} = 160 \times \frac{5}{4} = 200\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(100, 120, 200) = 600\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 3$$
$$\text{Rate of }(B + C) = 5 + 3 = 8,\quad \text{Rate of }(A + C) = 6 + 3 = 9$$
$$\frac{8x}{9(x - 41)} = \frac{19}{6} \implies 48x = 171x - 7011$$
$$123x = 7011 \implies x = 57$$
$$\text{Work done by C alone in } 2x = 114\text{ days} = 114 \times 3 = 342\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Fraction} = \frac{342}{600} = \frac{57}{100}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Ramesh does half as much work as Parul in $\frac{4}{5}$ of the time. If together Ramesh and Parul take 24 days to complete the work, then how much time will Parul take to do it?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let Parul's efficiency be } P \text{ and Ramesh's efficiency be } R.$$
$$R \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{2} P \implies R = \frac{5}{8} P \implies \frac{R}{P} = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 + 8) \times 24 = 13 \times 24 = 312\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Parul alone} = \frac{312}{8} = 39\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Babita is 1.25 times as efficient as Deepak. Working together the duo can complete a piece of work in 40 days. In how many days can Deepak alone complete the same piece of work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Babita : Deepak} = 1.25 : 1 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Total work} = 9 \times 40 = 360\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Deepak alone} = \frac{360}{4} = 90\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Sapna is double efficient as compared to Rakesh. If they both work together on a project and complete it in 48 days, then the number of days in which Sapna alone can complete the project is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Sapna : Rakesh} = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 48 = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Sapna alone} = \frac{144}{2} = 72\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Teena does half of a task in 6 days. Later, with shyam's help, she completes the ramaining work in 4 days. Shyam alone can finish the entire work in:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Teena can complete the whole work in } 6 \times 2 = 12\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Teena and Shyam together can complete remaining half in 4 days } \implies \text{entire work in } 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ days.}$$
$$\frac{1}{\text{Shyam}} = \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3 - 2}{24} = \frac{1}{24}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Shyam alone} = 24\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Joy completed the school project in 15 days. How many days will Tim take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Joy?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiency Tim : Joy} = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Time ratio Tim : Joy} = 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tim} = 15 \times \frac{4}{5} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiency Amit : Nirmal} = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Time ratio Amit : Nirmal} = 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Time taken by Amit} = 45 \times \frac{4}{5} = 36\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Arvind works 4 times as fast as Suresh. If Suresh can complete a work in 20 days independently, then find the number of days in which Arvind and Suresh can together finish the work.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiency of Suresh} = 1,\quad \text{Efficiency of Arvind} = 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 1 \times 20 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{20}{5} = 4\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Tarun is twice as good as Tripti in doing a work. Together, they can complete the work in 16 days. In how many days can Tripti alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiency of Tarun : Tripti} = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 16 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tripti alone} = \frac{48}{1} = 48\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: P is two times efficient than Q. P is able to complete a piece of work in 40 days less than Q. Working together, the whole number of days taken by them to complete the work is: (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } P : Q = 2 : 1 \implies \text{Time ratio } P : Q = 1 : 2$$
$$\text{Difference in time} = 2x - x = x = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P} = 40\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Q} = 80\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{80}{2 + 1} = \frac{80}{3} = 26.67 \approx 27\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: X alone can complete a work in 18 days and Y alone can do the same work in half time of the time taken by X. Working together what part of the same work they can complete in a day?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time taken by X} = 18\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Y} = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by X in 1 day} = \frac{1}{18}$$
$$\text{Work done by Y in 1 day} = \frac{1}{9}$$
$$\text{Work done together in 1 day} = \frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1 + 2}{18} = \frac{3}{18} = \frac{1}{6}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Raj alone can complete a work in 20 days and Pratap alone can complete the same work in half of the time taken by Raj. In how many days, will both together complete $\frac{3}{5}$ part of the total work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time taken by Raj} = 20\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Pratap} = 10\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 10) = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Raj} = 1,\quad \text{Efficiency of Pratap} = 2$$
$$\text{Required work} = \frac{3}{5} \times 20 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{12}{1 + 2} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 48 days. A is 4 times as efficient as B. In how many days B alone can complete the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } A : B = 4 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$\text{Total work} = 5 \times 48 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{240}{1} = 240\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: R can finish a work in 6 days if he works 10 hours a day. S can finish it in 5 days if he works 8 hours a day. If both start a work and work daily for 6 hours, the work will be finished in days.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total hours for R} = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total hours for S} = 5 \times 8 = 40\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(60, 40) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{120}{60} = 2\text{ units/hour},\quad \text{Efficiency of S} = \frac{120}{40} = 3\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Combined hourly rate} = 2 + 3 = 5\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Total hours needed} = \frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Days required (at 6 hours/day)} = \frac{24}{6} = 4\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: If 6 engineers can complete a work in 5 days and 5 skilled workers can complete the same work in 7 days, then the time taken (in days) to complete the same work by 7 engineers and 4 skilled workers will be
questions.solution:
$$6E \times 5 = 5S \times 7 \implies 30E = 35S \implies 6E = 7S \implies \frac{E}{S} = \frac{7}{6}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 30 \times 7 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 7E + 4S = 7(7) + 4(6) = 49 + 24 = 73\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{210}{73} = 2\frac{64}{73}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: To finish a work, P takes half of the number of days required by Q to finish it. If they together can finish the work in 36 days, then in how many days Q alone can finish the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } P : Q = 1 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } P : Q = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 36 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Q alone} = \frac{108}{1} = 108\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A work can be done by a man and a woman in 12 days and 8 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be done by 6 men and 4 women?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Rate of 1 man} = \frac{1}{12},\quad \text{Rate of 1 woman} = \frac{1}{8}$$
$$\text{Rate of 6 men and 4 women} = 6 \times \frac{1}{12} + 4 \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1}{1} = 1\text{ day}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
questions.solution:
$$4M = 6B \implies 2M = 3B \implies \frac{M}{B} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4(3) \times 20 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6M + 11B = 6(3) + 11(2) = 18 + 22 = 40\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{40} = 6\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: If 2 men or 4 women can build a wall in 34 days, in how many days can 6 men and 5 women build the same wall?
questions.solution:
$$2M = 4W \implies 1M = 2W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 2(2) \times 34 = 136\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6M + 5W = 6(2) + 5(1) = 12 + 5 = 17\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{136}{17} = 8\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Working 5 hours a day, A can complete a task in 8 days and working 6 hours a day, B can finish the same task in 10 days. Working 8 hours a day, they can jointly complete the task in _____.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total hours for A} = 5 \times 8 = 40\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total hours for B} = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(40, 60) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{120}{40} = 3\text{ units/hour},\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{120}{60} = 2\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Combined hourly rate} = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Total hours required} = \frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Days required (at 8 hours/day)} = \frac{24}{8} = 3\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A alone can finish a work in 15 days. A works only for the first two days and last two days. The rest work is done by B and the work is completed in 20 days. In how many days A and B together can finish the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let total work} = 60\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{60}{15} = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{A worked for } 2 + 2 = 4\text{ days } \implies \text{work done by A} = 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 16 = 44\text{ units, completed by B in } 20 - 4 = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{44}{16} = \frac{11}{4}\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + \frac{11}{4} = \frac{27}{4}\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{60}{27/4} = \frac{240}{27} = \frac{80}{9}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: After working alone for 12 days, Reena finds that only 10 percent of the work is completed. She employs Priya who is 40 percent more efficient than Reena. How many more days will they together take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Reena completes 10% in 12 days } \implies \text{total time for Reena} = 120\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Let total work} = 120\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of Reena} = 1$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 90\% \times 120 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Priya} = 1 + 0.40 = 1.4$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 1.4 = 2.4$$
$$\text{Days taken for remaining work} = \frac{108}{2.4} = 45\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A can do a piece of work in 25 days. After working for 5 days, he took help of B and completed the work in 8 days. If both A and B had worked together from the beginning, in how many days would they have completed the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let total work} = 100\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{100}{25} = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 5 days} = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100 - 20 = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of }(A + B) = \frac{80}{8} = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken together from beginning} = \frac{100}{10} = 10\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Naman does half of the work as Gagan in $\frac{4}{5}$ time. If together they take 16 days to complete a piece of work, then how long will Gagan take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let Gagan's efficiency be } G \text{ and Naman's efficiency be } N.$$
$$N \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{2} G \implies N = \frac{5}{8} G \implies \frac{N}{G} = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 + 8) \times 16 = 13 \times 16 = 208\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Gagan alone} = \frac{208}{8} = 26\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: P can do one-fourth piece of some work in 18 days. She completed 37.5% of that work and left it. Q completed the remaining work in 40 days. Working together they will complete $\frac{17}{48}$ part of the same work in:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total days for P} = 18 \times 4 = 72\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100\% - 37.5\% = 62.5\% = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total days for Q} = 40 \times \frac{8}{5} = 64\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(72, 64) = 576\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{576}{72} = 8,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{576}{64} = 9$$
$$\text{Work to complete} = \frac{17}{48} \times 576 = 17 \times 12 = 204\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{204}{8 + 9} = \frac{204}{17} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: To do a certain work, efficiencies of A and B are in the ratio $7 : 5$. Working together, they can complete the work in $17\frac{1}{2}$ days. In how many days, will B alone complete 50% of the same work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies of A and B} = 7 : 5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 7 + 5 = 12$$
$$\text{Total work} = 12 \times 17.5 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{50% of the work} = \frac{210}{2} = 105\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{105}{5} = 21\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Amita can build a room in the same amount of time that Bina and Sita working together can build. If Amita and Bina together could do it in 25 days and Sita alone in 35 days, then how many days are required for Bina alone to do the same work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Given: } E_A = E_B + E_S$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(25, 35) = 175\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{175}{25} = 7,\quad E_S = \frac{175}{35} = 5$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_S = 7 + 5 = 12$$
$$\text{Since } E_A = E_B + E_S, \text{ we have } 2E_A = 12 \implies E_A = 6$$
$$E_B = 7 - 6 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by Bina alone} = \frac{175}{1} = 175\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Robert takes twice as much time as Tom and thrice as much time as Jeorge to complete a work. If working together, they can complete it in 23 hours, then find the time that Tom will take to complete the work.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } T_R : T_T : T_J = 6 : 3 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } E_R : E_T : E_J = 1 : 2 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6 \times 23 = 138\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tom} = \frac{138}{2} = 69\text{ hours}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A takes twice as much time as B and thrice as much time as C to finalise a task. Working together, they can complete the task in 8 days. The time (in days) taken by A, B and C, respectively, to complete the task is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } T_A : T_B : T_C = 6 : 3 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } E_A : E_B : E_C = 1 : 2 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A} = \frac{48}{1} = 48\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B} = \frac{48}{2} = 24\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by C} = \frac{48}{3} = 16\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days. B and C together can do it in 30 days. If A is twice as efficient as C then in how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 30) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$A + B = \frac{90}{18} = 5,\quad B + C = \frac{90}{30} = 3$$
$$(A + B) - (B + C) = A - C = 5 - 3 = 2$$
$$\text{Given } A = 2C \implies 2C - C = C = 2$$
$$B = 3 - C = 3 - 2 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{90}{1} = 90\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: The ratio of work efficiency of A, B and C is $2 : 5 : 3$. Working together, they can complete a work in 27 days. In how many days will B and C together complete $\frac{4}{9}$ parts of the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies of A, B, C} = 2 : 5 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 5 + 3 = 10$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 27 = 270\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required work} = \frac{4}{9} \times 270 = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined rate of B and C} = 5 + 3 = 8$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{120}{8} = 15\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: The ratio of work efficiency of A, B and C is $2 : 3 : 5$. Working together, they can complete a work in 6 days. In how many days will A complete 20% of the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 6 = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{20% of work} = \frac{20}{100} \times 60 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 2$$
$$\text{Time taken by A} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A can do a certain piece of work in 2.4 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do the same piece of work in 27 days and C alone can do it in 75 days, then how many days will B take to do this piece of work alone?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{T_A}{T_{B+C}} = 2.4 = \frac{12}{5} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_{B+C}} = \frac{5}{12} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_A + E_B + E_C} = \frac{5}{17}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(27, 75) = 675\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{675}{27} = 25,\quad E_C = \frac{675}{75} = 9$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_C = 25 + 9 = 34$$
$$E_A = 34 \times \frac{5}{17} = 10$$
$$E_B = 25 - 10 = 15$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{675}{15} = 45\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A & B can do a piece of work in 10 days. B and C can do the same work in 15 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, find in what time B alone can do the work (in days).
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$A + B = \frac{30}{10} = 3,\quad B + C = \frac{30}{15} = 2$$
$$(A + B) - (B + C) = A - C = 3 - 2 = 1$$
$$\text{Since } A = 2C \implies 2C - C = C = 1$$
$$B = 2 - C = 2 - 1 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{30}{1} = 30\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A can do a certain piece of work in 1.5 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do the same piece of work in 30 days and C alone can do it in 120 days, then how many days will B take to do this piece of work alone?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{T_A}{T_{B+C}} = 1.5 = \frac{3}{2} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_{B+C}} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_A + E_B + E_C} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 120) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{120}{30} = 4,\quad E_C = \frac{120}{120} = 1$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_C = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$E_A = 5 \times \frac{2}{5} = 2$$
$$E_B = 4 - 2 = 2$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{120}{2} = 60\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: To do a certain task X would take 3 times as long as Y and Z together; and Z would takes 4 times as long as Y and X together. Three of them together can complete the task in 10 days. How much time is taken by X and Z to complete the task?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{E_X}{E_{Y+Z}} = \frac{1}{3} \implies E_X = \frac{1}{4}(E_X + E_Y + E_Z)$$
$$\frac{E_Z}{E_{X+Y}} = \frac{1}{4} \implies E_Z = \frac{1}{5}(E_X + E_Y + E_Z)$$
$$\text{Let total efficiency } E = 20.$$
$$E_X = \frac{20}{4} = 5,\quad E_Z = \frac{20}{5} = 4$$
$$E_X + E_Z = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 10 = 200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by X and Z together} = \frac{200}{9} = 22\frac{2}{9}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A alone can do 2/5 of a work in 12 days. B is 25 percent more efficient than A. C alone can do the same work in 12 days less than B. D is 25 percent less efficient than C. If they all work together, then the work will be completed in how many days?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time for A} = 12 \times \frac{5}{2} = 30\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for B} = \frac{30}{1.25} = 24\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for C} = 24 - 12 = 12\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for D} = \frac{12}{0.75} = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 24, 12, 16) = 240\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 8,\quad E_B = 10,\quad E_C = 20,\quad E_D = 15$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 8 + 10 + 20 + 15 = 53$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{240}{53}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: To do a certain work, A is 40% more efficient than B. Working together, they can do the same work in 15 days. A started the work and left after 15 days. B and C together completed the remaining work in next 10 days. C alone can do one third of the original work in:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{E_A}{E_B} = \frac{140}{100} = \frac{7}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (7 + 5) \times 15 = 12 \times 15 = 180\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 15 days} = 7 \times 15 = 105\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 180 - 105 = 75\text{ units}$$
$$E_B + E_C = \frac{75}{10} = 7.5 \implies 5 + E_C = 7.5 \implies E_C = 2.5$$
$$\text{One-third of total work} = \frac{180}{3} = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by C alone} = \frac{60}{2.5} = 24\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A can complete a work in $11\frac{1}{2}$ days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 50% as efficient as B. Working together A, B and C will complete the same work
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time for A} = \frac{23}{2}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Let } E_A = 4. \quad \text{Total work} = 4 \times \frac{23}{2} = 46\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 4 = 5$$
$$E_C = 0.50 \times 5 = 2.5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 5 + 2.5 = 11.5 = \frac{23}{2}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{46}{23/2} = 4\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A does a work in 15 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 40% more efficient than B. A and C work together for 3 days and then C leaves. A and B together complete the remaining work:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let } E_A = 20. \quad \text{Total work} = 20 \times 15 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 20 = 25$$
$$E_C = 1.40 \times 25 = 35$$
$$\text{Work done by A and C in 3 days} = (20 + 35) \times 3 = 165\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 300 - 165 = 135\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of }(A + B) = 20 + 25 = 45$$
$$\text{Time taken by A and B} = \frac{135}{45} = 3\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A can complete a work in 40 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 28% more efficient than B. They work together for 5 days. How many days will B alone take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let } E_A = 20. \quad \text{Total work} = 20 \times 40 = 800\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 20 = 25$$
$$E_C = 1.28 \times 25 = 32$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 20 + 25 + 32 = 77$$
$$\text{Work done in 5 days} = 77 \times 5 = 385\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 800 - 385 = 415\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{415}{25} = \frac{83}{5} = 16\frac{3}{5}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: To complete a certain work, X is 40% more efficient than Y and Z is 40% less efficient than Y. Working together, they can complete the work in 21 days. Y and Z worked together for 35 days. In how many days will X alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let } E_Y = 10 \implies E_X = 14,\quad E_Z = 6$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 14 + 10 + 6 = 30$$
$$\text{Total work} = 30 \times 21 = 630\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by Y and Z in 35 days} = (10 + 6) \times 35 = 16 \times 35 = 560\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 630 - 560 = 70\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by X alone} = \frac{70}{14} = 5\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A's efficiency is twice that of B's. A can work only for 8 hours a day while B can work for 12 hours a day. If A can finish a work in 12 days, in how many days can B finish the same work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Hourly efficiency ratio } A : B = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Daily work of A} = 2 \times 8 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16 \times 12 = 192\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Daily work of B} = 1 \times 12 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days taken by B} = \frac{192}{12} = 16\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 30, 40) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$P + Q = 5,\quad Q + R = 4,\quad P + R = 3$$
$$2(P + Q + R) = 12 \implies P + Q + R = 6$$
$$P = 6 - 4 = 2,\quad Q = 6 - 3 = 3,\quad R = 6 - 5 = 1$$
$$X = 4P = 8,\quad Y = 0.5Q = 1.5,\quad Z = 2.5R = 2.5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of } X + Y + Z = 8 + 1.5 + 2.5 = 12$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{120}{12} = 10\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A, B and C can finish a work in 15 days working alternately in the same order. The efficiency of A is the same as that of B, and the efficiency of C is equal to that of A. In how many days will the work be finished if they work alternately in the order C, A and B?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Given that } E_A = E_B = E_C.$$
$$\text{Since all three individuals have identical efficiencies, any permutation of their alternate order will yield identical daily progress.}$$
$$\text{Therefore, working alternately in the order C, A, B will take the exact same } 15\text{ days.}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: Abha and Anuj working together completed a job in $\frac{40}{9}$ days. If Abha had worked twice as efficiently as she actually did and Anuj had worked $\frac{1}{3}$ of his actual efficiency, then the work would have been completed in $\frac{60}{17}$ days. Find the time Abha would take to complete the work alone.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let Abha's rate be } A \text{ and Anuj's rate be } B.$$
$$A + B = \frac{9}{40} W$$
$$2A + \frac{1}{3}B = \frac{17}{60} W$$
$$\text{Multiplying first equation by } \frac{1}{3}: \quad \frac{1}{3}A + \frac{1}{3}B = \frac{3}{40} W$$
$$\text{Subtracting: } \left(2 - \frac{1}{3}\right)A = \frac{17}{60} - \frac{3}{40}$$
$$\frac{5}{3} A = \frac{34 - 9}{120} = \frac{25}{120} = \frac{5}{24}$$
$$A = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{24} = \frac{1}{8} W$$
$$\text{Time taken by Abha alone} = 8\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: CONCEPT OF EFFICIENCY
questions.questionText: A, B and C together can complete a work in $x$, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 45) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = \frac{90}{30} = 3,\quad E_C = \frac{90}{45} = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by B and C in 6 days} = (3 + 2) \times 6 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 90 - 30 = 60\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = \frac{60}{12} = 5\text{ units/day}$$
$$x = \frac{90}{5} = 18\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 55 Workers can finish a work in 16 days. For finishing the same work in 10 days, how many more workers are required?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 55 \times 16 = 880\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Total workers required for 10 days} = \frac{880}{10} = 88$$
$$\text{Additional workers required} = 88 - 55 = 33$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 47 masons can dig a 35 m long trench in one day. How many masons should be employed for digging a 105m long trench of the same type in one day?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{M_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2}{W_2} \implies \frac{47}{35} = \frac{M_2}{105}$$
$$M_2 = \frac{47 \times 105}{35} = 47 \times 3 = 141\text{ masons}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: If 7 men working 8 hours a day for 5 day's can complete a work, then how many men are required to complete the same work if they work 10 hours a day for 7 days?
questions.solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$7 \times 5 \times 8 = M_2 \times 7 \times 10$$
$$280 = 70 M_2 \implies M_2 = \frac{280}{70} = 4\text{ men}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 16 men can dig a ditch 24 m long in 18 days, working 6 hours a day. How many more men should be engaged to dig a similar ditch 42 m long in 9 days, each man now working 12 hours per day?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{16 \times 18 \times 6}{24} = \frac{M_2 \times 9 \times 12}{42}$$
$$72 = \frac{18 M_2}{7} \implies M_2 = \frac{72 \times 7}{18} = 28\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Additional men required} = 28 - 16 = 12$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: Eighteen persons working 8 hours a day can complete 3 units of work in 10 days. How many days are required by 25 persons to complete 5 units of work working 6 hours a day?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{18 \times 10 \times 8}{3} = \frac{25 \times D_2 \times 6}{5}$$
$$480 = 30 D_2 \implies D_2 = \frac{480}{30} = 16\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 18 men can complete $\frac{1}{5}$ of a work in 10 days. How many people are required to complete $\frac{2}{5}$ of the same work in 5 days?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{18 \times 10}{1/5} = \frac{M_2 \times 5}{2/5}$$
$$180 \times 5 = \frac{5 M_2}{2/5} \implies 18 \times 10 \times 2 = 5 M_2$$
$$360 = 5 M_2 \implies M_2 = 72\text{ people}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 30 men working 5 hours a day can do work in 18 days. In how many days will 20 men working 7 hours a day do the same work?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: Twelve men working for 9 hours a day complete a piece of work in 24 days. In how many days can 8 men working for 12 hours a day complete the same piece of work?
questions.solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$12 \times 24 \times 9 = 8 \times D_2 \times 12$$
$$24 \times 9 = 8 D_2 \implies 216 = 8 D_2 \implies D_2 = 27\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: Eight laborers working 10 hours a day completed a work in 18 days. If only 5 laborers are working, then in how many hours a day should they work to finish the work in 24 days?
questions.solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$8 \times 18 \times 10 = 5 \times 24 \times H_2$$
$$1440 = 120 H_2 \implies H_2 = \frac{1440}{120} = 12\text{ hours/day}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 30 persons working 10 hours a day can do 5 units of work in 12 days. How many people are required to do 8 units of that work in 16 days if they work for 8 hours a day?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{30 \times 12 \times 10}{5} = \frac{M_2 \times 16 \times 8}{8}$$
$$720 = 16 M_2 \implies M_2 = \frac{720}{16} = 45\text{ people}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: A group of 25 tourists consume 5 containers of food in 8 days in a hotel. How many containers will be required for 10 tourists to eat for 16 days?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{T_1 \times D_1}{C_1} = \frac{T_2 \times D_2}{C_2}$$
$$\frac{25 \times 8}{5} = \frac{10 \times 16}{C_2}$$
$$40 = \frac{160}{C_2} \implies C_2 = \frac{160}{40} = 4\text{ containers}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days will 24 persons, working 9 hours a day complete the work?
questions.solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$36 \times 10 \times 6 = 24 \times D_2 \times 9$$
$$2160 = 216 D_2 \implies D_2 = \frac{2160}{216} = 10\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 36 equally efficient workers can paint 25 identical walls in 48 days. In how many days can 45 such workers paint 60 such walls?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 100 workers working 8 hours a day can dig a canal 2000 metres long in 25 days. Find the number of workers required to dig a similar canal of 2800 metres long in 32 days working 5 hours a day.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: In a camp of 70 boys, there are food provisions for 36 days. If 50 boys join the camp, then how many days will the provisions last?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total provisions} = 70 \times 36 = 2520\text{ boy-days}$$
$$\text{New strength} = 70 + 50 = 120\text{ boys}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{2520}{120} = 21\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: In an army camp, there is food provision for 500 cadets for 25 days. If 125 more persons join the army camp on the first day itself, then for how many days will the provision last?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total provisions} = 500 \times 25 = 12500\text{ cadet-days}$$
$$\text{New strength} = 500 + 125 = 625\text{ cadets}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{12500}{625} = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 30 men can complete a work in 12 days. After 6 days, 24 more men joined them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Remaining work for 30 men} = 30 \times (12 - 6) = 180\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Total men working} = 30 + 24 = 54\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{180}{54} = \frac{10}{3} = 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: 10 men can do a work in 25 days. After 12 days of work, 3 more men were engaged to finish the work. The number of days required to complete the remaining work is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Remaining work for 10 men} = 10 \times (25 - 12) = 130\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Total men engaged} = 10 + 3 = 13\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required for remaining work} = \frac{130}{13} = 10\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: Working for 10 hours per day, 6 men can build a wall in a certain number of days. By working for how many hours per day can 12 men build the wall in the same days?
questions.solution:
$$M_1 H_1 D = M_2 H_2 D$$
$$6 \times 10 = 12 \times H_2$$
$$60 = 12 H_2 \implies H_2 = \frac{60}{12} = 5\text{ hours}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: A group of men committed to completing a task in 20 days. The work was completed in 40 days because 5 workers did not come for work. Determine the number of men who originally agreed to do the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let the original number of men be } M.$$
$$M \times 20 = (M - 5) \times 40$$
$$20M = 40M - 200 \implies 20M = 200 \implies M = 10\text{ men}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: A work can be completed by N men in 15 days. 5 men leave the work after 3 days. The remaining work was completed in 18 days. What is the value of N?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 15N$$
$$15N = 3N + (N - 5) \times 18$$
$$15N = 3N + 18N - 90$$
$$15N = 21N - 90 \implies 6N = 90 \implies N = 15$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: MDH CONCEPT
questions.questionText: To finish a work in 12 days, 8 workers are engaged. After 2 days, due to some urgency, the work is to be finished in next 2 days. How many more workers are to be engaged now to finish it on time?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Remaining work} = 8 \times (12 - 2) = 80\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Workers required to finish in 2 days} = \frac{80}{2} = 40\text{ workers}$$
$$\text{Additional workers to be engaged} = 40 - 8 = 32$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 18 workers can complete a piece of work in 96 days. They start working together and after 26 days 10 more workers join them. In how many days in all will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Remaining work after 26 days} = 18 \times (96 - 26) = 18 \times 70 = 1260\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Total workers now} = 18 + 10 = 28\text{ workers}$$
$$\text{Time required for remaining work} = \frac{1260}{28} = 45\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days in all} = 26 + 45 = 71\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: A hostel had food provision for 300 students for a month. After 20 days, 50 students left the hostel. How long would the remaining food last? (1 month = 30 days)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Remaining provision} = 300 \times (30 - 20) = 3000\text{ student-days}$$
$$\text{Remaining students} = 300 - 50 = 250\text{ students}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{3000}{250} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: A work can be finished by 8 men in 10 days working 6 hours a day or same can be finished by 20 qualified workers in 6 days working 8 hours a day. 2 men and 4 qualified workers work simultaneously 10 hours a day, the work will be finished in ____ days.
questions.solution:
$$8M \times 10 \times 6 = 20Q \times 6 \times 8 \implies 480M = 960Q \implies 1M = 2Q$$
$$\text{Total work} = 480 \times 2 = 960\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Hourly rate of } 2M + 4Q = 2(2) + 4(1) = 8\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Daily rate (10 hours/day)} = 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{960}{80} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: In an office, 75 employees can finish a project in 60 days. After few days, 15 employees left the job and the project was completed in 65 days. After how many days did the 15 employees leave?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 75 \times 60 = 4500\text{ employee-days}$$
$$\text{Let they leave after } x \text{ days.}$$
$$75x + (75 - 15)(65 - x) = 4500$$
$$75x + 60(65 - x) = 4500$$
$$75x + 3900 - 60x = 4500$$
$$15x = 600 \implies x = 40\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: $(N + 18)$ persons, each working for 7.5 hours a day, can complete 48% of a work in 20 days. $(N + 12)$ persons can complete the remaining work in 30 days, if each of them works for 6.5 hours per day. Determine the value of N.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 20 men can complete a piece of work in 40 days, and 40 women can do the same work in 60 days. If 10 men and 20 women work together, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$20M \times 40 = 40W \times 60 \implies 800M = 2400W \implies 1M = 3W$$
$$\text{Total work} = 800 \times 3 = 2400\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 10M + 20W = 10(3) + 20(1) = 50\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{2400}{50} = 48\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 15 men can complete a work in 25 days, and 25 women can complete the same work in 40 days. If all the 15 men and 25 women work together, in how many days will the work get completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Daily rate of 15 men} = \frac{1}{25},\quad \text{Daily rate of 25 women} = \frac{1}{40}$$
$$\text{Combined daily rate} = \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{40} = \frac{8 + 5}{200} = \frac{13}{200}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{200}{13} = 15\frac{5}{13}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 15 men and 25 women can complete a piece of work in 9.6 days. If 16 women can complete the same work in 27 days, find the number of days in which 16 men can complete the same work.
questions.solution:
$$(15M + 25W) \times 9.6 = 16W \times 27$$
$$144M + 240W = 432W \implies 144M = 192W \implies 3M = 4W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{4}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16(3) \times 27 = 1296\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 16 men} = 16 \times 4 = 64\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1296}{64} = \frac{81}{4} = 20.25\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days. The same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women. How many days will it take to complete when 4 men and 4 women are employed to perform the same job?
questions.solution:
$$8M \times 10 = 10W \times 12 \implies 80M = 120W \implies 2M = 3W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 8(3) \times 10 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W = 4(3) + 4(2) = 12 + 8 = 20\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{20} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 10 women can do a work in 6 days and 6 men can do the same work in 5 days. If all these men and women work together, then how many days will they take to finish this work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Daily rate of 10 women} = \frac{1}{6},\quad \text{Daily rate of 6 men} = \frac{1}{5}$$
$$\text{Combined daily rate} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{11}{30}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{30}{11} = 2\frac{8}{11}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 2 men can finish a work in 6 days and 3 women can finish the same work in 4 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 1 man and 2 women, working together every day?
questions.solution:
$$2M \times 6 = 3W \times 4 \implies 12M = 12W \implies 1M = 1W$$
$$\text{Total work} = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 2W = 1 + 2 = 3\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 12 men can do a work is 8 days while 4 boys can do it in 40 days. In how many days 9 boys and 3 men together will complete the same work?
questions.solution:
$$12M \times 8 = 4B \times 40 \implies 96M = 160B \implies 3M = 5B \implies \frac{M}{B} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 96 \times 5 = 480\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 3M + 9B = 3(5) + 9(3) = 15 + 27 = 42\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{480}{42} = \frac{80}{7}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 4 men and 7 women can do a work in 8 days. 7 men and 4 women can do the same work in 5 days. Find the number of days in which 8 women can finish the work?
questions.solution:
$$(4M + 7W) \times 8 = (7M + 4W) \times 5$$
$$32M + 56W = 35M + 20W \implies 3M = 36W \implies 1M = 12W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 12 + 7) \times 8 = 55 \times 8 = 440\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 8 women} = 8\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{440}{8} = 55\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: If 6 women can complete a work in 3 days, and 9 girls can complete the same work in 2 days, then find the time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls?
questions.solution:
$$6W \times 3 = 9G \times 2 \implies 18W = 18G \implies 1W = 1G$$
$$\text{Total work} = 18\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 8W + 6G = 8 + 6 = 14\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{18}{14} = \frac{9}{7}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days. While 6 men and 14 women in 5 days. In how many days will 20 women finish the job?
questions.solution:
$$(8M + 12W) \times 4 = (6M + 14W) \times 5$$
$$32M + 48W = 30M + 70W \implies 2M = 22W \implies 1M = 11W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (8 \times 11 + 12) \times 4 = 100 \times 4 = 400\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 20 women} = 20\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{400}{20} = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: Sixteen men can complete a work in 8 days. Eight men and nine women working together can complete the same work in 10 days. In how many days will 20 women complete this work?
questions.solution:
$$16M \times 8 = (8M + 9W) \times 10$$
$$128M = 80M + 90W \implies 48M = 90W \implies 8M = 15W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{15}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16(15) \times 8 = 1920\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 20 women} = 20 \times 8 = 160\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1920}{160} = 12\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 3 men can finish a work in 10 days, 4 women can finish it in 12 days and 10 qualified workers can finish it in 6 days. In how many days is the work finished by 4 men, 4 women and 4 qualified workers, working together every day?
questions.solution:
$$3M \times 10 = 4W \times 12 = 10Q \times 6 = \text{Total Work}$$
$$30M = 48W = 60Q = 240\text{ units}$$
$$M = 8,\quad W = 5,\quad Q = 4$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W + 4Q = 4(8) + 4(5) + 4(4) = 32 + 20 + 16 = 68\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{68} = \frac{60}{17}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 4 men and 8 women complete a job in 10 days and 5 men and 24 women complete the same work in 4 days. In how many days will 1 man and 1 women complete the same work?
questions.solution:
$$(4M + 8W) \times 10 = (5M + 24W) \times 4$$
$$40M + 80W = 20M + 96W \implies 20M = 16W \implies 5M = 4W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{4}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 4 + 8 \times 5) \times 10 = 56 \times 10 = 560\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{560}{9} = 62\frac{2}{9}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
