questions.questionText: 15 men and 21 women, working together, can do a job in 56 days, while 12 men and 24 women, working together, can do the same job in 64 days. In how many days can the same job be done by 18 men and 24 women, working together?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: A man and a woman can finish a work together in half the time taken by a woman and a boy together. A boy can finish the work alone in 20 days and 2 women together can finish it in 30 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 4 men?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Time for 1 boy} = 20\text{ days},\quad \text{Time for 1 woman} = 30 \times 2 = 60\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 60\text{ units} \implies E_B = 3,\quad E_W = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by woman and boy} = \frac{60}{1 + 3} = 15\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by man and woman} = \frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ days}$$
$$E_M + E_W = \frac{60}{7.5} = 8 \implies E_M = 8 - 1 = 7$$
$$\text{Rate of 4 men} = 4 \times 7 = 28\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{60}{28} = \frac{15}{7} \approx 2.14\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 4 men's work is equal to 6 women's work, and 4 women's work is equal to 6 boys' work. A boy can finish the work in 60 days. In how many days can the work be finished by a man and a woman together?
questions.solution:
$$4M = 6W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{6}$$
$$4W = 6B \implies \frac{W}{B} = \frac{3}{2} = \frac{6}{4}$$
$$M : W : B = 9 : 6 : 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4 \times 60 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W = 9 + 6 = 15\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{15} = 16\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 10 women take 16 days to complete a work which can be completed by 6 men in 8 days. 12 men started working and after 2 days 6 men left, and 5 women joined them. In how many days will the work be completed ?
questions.solution:
$$10W \times 16 = 6M \times 8 \implies 160W = 48M \implies 10W = 3M \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{10}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6(10) \times 8 = 480\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by 12 men in 2 days} = 12(10) \times 2 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 480 - 240 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New rate of 6 men and 5 women} = 6(10) + 5(3) = 60 + 15 = 75\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining days} = \frac{240}{75} = \frac{16}{5}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete work} = 2 + \frac{16}{5} = \frac{26}{5}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 1 man and 4 women can complete a work in $\frac{65}{4}$ days, while 3 men and 4 women can complete it in $\frac{13}{2}$ days. In how many days will 13 women complete the same.
questions.solution:
$$(1M + 4W) \times \frac{65}{4} = (3M + 4W) \times \frac{13}{2}$$
$$\text{Dividing both sides by } \frac{13}{4}: \quad 5(1M + 4W) = 2(3M + 4W)$$
$$5M + 20W = 6M + 8W \implies 1M = 12W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{12}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (12 + 4) \times \frac{65}{4} = 16 \times \frac{65}{4} = 260\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 13 women} = 13 \times 1 = 13\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{260}{13} = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 25 men and 45 women can complete a piece of work in 15 days, while 15 men and 60 women can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can 69 men and 67 women complete the work?
questions.solution:
$$15(25M + 45W) = 20(15M + 60W)$$
$$3(25M + 45W) = 4(15M + 60W)$$
$$75M + 135W = 60M + 240W \implies 15M = 105W \implies 1M = 7W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (25 \times 7 + 45) \times 15 = 220 \times 15 = 3300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 69M + 67W = 69(7) + 67(1) = 483 + 67 = 550\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{3300}{550} = 6\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: A project can be completed by 2 men and 5 women in 8 days while 4 men and 6 women can complete the same project in 5 days. How many men will be required to complete this project in 4 days?
questions.solution:
$$8(2M + 5W) = 5(4M + 6W)$$
$$16M + 40W = 20M + 30W \implies 4M = 10W \implies 2M = 5W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{5}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (2 \times 5 + 5 \times 2) \times 8 = 20 \times 8 = 160\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 4 days} = \frac{160}{4} = 40\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Men required} = \frac{40}{5} = 8\text{ men}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 5 men and 2 boys can do in 30 days as much work as 7 men and 10 boys can do in 15 days. How many boys should join 40 men to do the same work in 4 days?
questions.solution:
$$30(5M + 2B) = 15(7M + 10B)$$
$$2(5M + 2B) = 7M + 10B$$
$$10M + 4B = 7M + 10B \implies 3M = 6B \implies 1M = 2B$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 \times 2 + 2) \times 30 = 12 \times 30 = 360\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 4 days} = \frac{360}{4} = 90\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by 40 men} = 40 \times 2 = 80\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining work for boys} = 90 - 80 = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Boys required} = \frac{10}{1} = 10\text{ boys}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 4 men and 5 women can complete a work in 15 days, whereas 9 men and 6 women can complete it in 10 days. To complete the same work in 7 days, how many women should assist 4 men?
questions.solution:
$$15(4M + 5W) = 10(9M + 6W)$$
$$3(4M + 5W) = 2(9M + 6W)$$
$$12M + 15W = 18M + 12W \implies 6M = 3W \implies 2M = 1W \implies \frac{W}{M} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 1 + 5 \times 2) \times 15 = 14 \times 15 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 7 days} = \frac{210}{7} = 30\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by 4 men} = 4 \times 1 = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining work for women} = 30 - 4 = 26\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Women required} = \frac{26}{2} = 13\text{ women}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: Five men can complete a work in 20 days. Ten women can complete the same work in 15 days. Two men and six women started working together. After 5 days, three women left the work and a new man joined the work. The group continued working together till the end of the work. In how many days will they be able to do the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$5M \times 20 = 10W \times 15 \implies 100M = 150W \implies 2M = 3W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 100 \times 3 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by 2 men and 6 women in 5 days} = [2(3) + 6(2)] \times 5 = 18 \times 5 = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 300 - 90 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New group: 3 men and 3 women} \implies \text{Rate} = 3(3) + 3(2) = 15\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time for remaining work} = \frac{210}{15} = 14\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 5 days, while 3 men and 4 women can complete it in 7 days. Similar how many men will have to help 25 women to complete $2\frac{1}{2}$ times the work in 5 days?
questions.solution:
$$5(4M + 6W) = 7(3M + 4W)$$
$$20M + 30W = 21M + 28W \implies 1M = 2W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Initial total work} = (4 \times 2 + 6 \times 1) \times 5 = 14 \times 5 = 70\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New work to complete} = 2.5 \times 70 = 175\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily rate for 5 days} = \frac{175}{5} = 35\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Rate of 25 women} = 25 \times 1 = 25\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining rate for men} = 35 - 25 = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Men required} = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ men}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: If 3 goats or 5 sheep can graze a field in 54 days, then in how many days can 6 goats and 8 sheep graze the same field?
questions.solution:
$$3G = 5S \implies \frac{G}{S} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3(5) \times 54 = 810\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6G + 8S = 6(5) + 8(3) = 30 + 24 = 54\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{810}{54} = 15\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: CONCEPT OF MWC
questions.questionText: If one man or two women or four boys or five girls can finish a work in 39 days, then how many days will one man, one woman, one boy and one girl together take to finish the same work?
questions.solution:
$$1M = 2W = 4B = 5G$$
$$\text{LCM}(1, 2, 4, 5) = 20 \implies M = 20,\quad W = 10,\quad B = 5,\quad G = 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 39 = 780\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W + 1B + 1G = 20 + 10 + 5 + 4 = 39\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{780}{39} = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: CONCEPT OF CONTRACTOR
questions.questionText: If 8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can do a piece of work in 8 months, then in how many months can 4 men, 4 women and 4 boys together complete the work?
questions.solution:
$$8M = 16W = 32B \implies 1M = 2W = 4B$$
$$\text{Efficiencies: } M = 4,\quad W = 2,\quad B = 1$$
$$\text{Total work} = 8(4) \times 8 = 256\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W + 4B = 4(4) + 4(2) + 4(1) = 16 + 8 + 4 = 28\text{ units/month}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{256}{28} = \frac{64}{7} = 9\frac{1}{7}\text{ months}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: CONCEPT OF CONTRACTOR
questions.questionText: The one-day work of 2 men is equal to the one-day work of 4 women or the one-day work of 8 qualified workers. 10 qualified workers can finish a work in 8 days. If a man, a woman and a qualified worker work in the same order on three different days, the work is finished in ____ days.
questions.solution:
$$2M = 4W = 8Q \implies 1M = 2W = 4Q$$
$$\text{Efficiencies: } M = 4,\quad W = 2,\quad Q = 1$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10(1) \times 8 = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In a 3-day cycle (Man, Woman, Worker), work done} = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done in } 11 \times 3 = 33\text{ days} = 11 \times 7 = 77\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 80 - 77 = 3\text{ units, to be done by Man (efficiency 4)}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = 33 + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{135}{4}\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: CONCEPT OF CONTRACTOR
questions.questionText: A contractor decided to complete a work in 80 days and employed 60 men at the beginning and 20 men additionally after 20 days and got the work completed as per schedule. If he had not employed the additional men, how many extra days would he have needed to complete the work (round off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 60 \times 20 + (60 + 20) \times (80 - 20) = 1200 + 80 \times 60 = 1200 + 4800 = 6000\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Time taken with original 60 men} = \frac{6000}{60} = 100\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Extra days needed} = 100 - 80 = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: CONCEPT OF CONTRACTOR
questions.questionText: A civil contractor planned to build an over bridge of 3 km distance in 600 days. For this purpose, he employed 90 workers. After 200 days of work, it was observed that only 0.5 km of the bridge was completed. What is the number of extra workers required to complete the work in time?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: CONCEPT OF AP IN TIME & WORK
questions.questionText: 60 men can complete a work in 40 days. They start work together but after every 10 day, 5 men leave the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 60 \times 40 = 2400\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 10: } 60 \times 10 = 600\text{ units (cumulative: 600)}$$
$$\text{Days 11 to 20: } 55 \times 10 = 550\text{ units (cumulative: 1150)}$$
$$\text{Days 21 to 30: } 50 \times 10 = 500\text{ units (cumulative: 1650)}$$
$$\text{Days 31 to 40: } 45 \times 10 = 450\text{ units (cumulative: 2100)}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 2400 - 2100 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Men available for next stretch} = 40\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{300}{40} = 7.5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 40 + 7.5 = 47.5\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: CONCEPT OF AP IN TIME & WORK
questions.questionText: Each one of five men independently can complete a work in 20 days. The work is started by one person. Next day one more person joins and every next day one more person joins. From the fifth day, five persons continued working as a team. In how many days, will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let rate of 1 person} = 1\text{ unit/day} \implies \text{Total work} = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done in first 4 days} = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{From day 5, rate of 5 persons} = 5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Additional days required} = \frac{10}{5} = 2\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 4 + 2 = 6\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: CONCEPT OF AP IN TIME & WORK
questions.questionText: A group of men decided to complete a job in 4 days. However, since 10 men dropped out every day, the job got completed at the end of the 7th day. How many men were there in the beginning?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let the initial number of men be } M.$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4M$$
$$\text{Work done in 7 days} = M + (M - 10) + (M - 20) + (M - 30) + (M - 40) + (M - 50) + (M - 60)$$
$$= 7M - 210$$
$$7M - 210 = 4M \implies 3M = 210 \implies M = 70\text{ men}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - X: MISCELLANEOUS QUESTIONS
questions.questionText: A and B working together can complete the work in d days. Working alone, A takes $(8 + d)$ and B takes $(18 + d)$ days to complete the same work. A works for 4 days, In how many days will B alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
$$d = \sqrt{8 \times 18} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = 8 + 12 = 20\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = 18 + 12 = 30\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 30) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 3,\quad E_B = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 4 days} = 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 12 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{48}{2} = 24\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - X: MISCELLANEOUS QUESTIONS
questions.questionText: When A alone does a piece of work, he takes 25 days more than the time taken by A and B to do the work together. On the other hand, B alone takes 16 days more than the time taken by A and B to do the work together. How many days will A and B, working together, take to do the work?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Let the time taken by A and B together be } T\text{ days.}$$
$$T = \sqrt{25 \times 16} = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - X: MISCELLANEOUS QUESTIONS
questions.questionText: Ten men begin to do a work. But after some days, four of them left the job. As a result, the job that could have been completed in 40 days is completed in 50 days. How many days after the commencement of the work did the four men leave?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 40 = 400\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Let 4 men leave after } x \text{ days.}$$
$$10x + (10 - 4)(50 - x) = 400$$
$$10x + 6(50 - x) = 400$$
$$10x + 300 - 6x = 400$$
$$4x = 100 \implies x = 25\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - X: MISCELLANEOUS QUESTIONS
questions.questionText: A work was finished by L, P and Q together. L and P together finished 50 percent part of the work and P and Q together finished 60 percent part of the work. Who among the three is most efficient?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - X: MISCELLANEOUS QUESTIONS
questions.questionText: Four persons, P Q, R, S were engaged for doing a task, with the condition that P; Q; R; S work, respectively, on (Mondays, Thursdays); (Tuesdays, Fridays); (Wednesdays, Saturdays); (Sundays). The task was began on a Monday, and got completed on the 15th day, which was also a Monday. If the efficiencies of P Q, R, S in respect of doing this task were in the proportion $1 : 2 : 3 : 4$, then in how many days could R complete the task, working alone without break?
questions.solution:
$$\text{In 14 days (2 full weeks):}$$
$$\text{P worked } 4\text{ days, Q worked } 4\text{ days, R worked } 4\text{ days, S worked } 2\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{On the 15th day (Monday), P worked 1 more day } \implies P\text{ worked } 5\text{ days total.}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 5(1) + 4(2) + 4(3) + 2(4) = 5 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 33\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = 3$$
$$\text{Days taken by R alone} = \frac{33}{3} = 11\text{ days}$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A and B undertake a project worth ₹36,000. A alone can do the work in 25 days. They worked together for 5 days. For the next five days, B worked alone. After that, A substituted B and completed the remaining work in 5 days. The share of A in the earnings is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total days A worked} = 5 + 5 = 10\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Since A alone completes the work in 25 days, fraction of work done by A} = \frac{10}{25} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Share of A} = \frac{2}{5} \times 36000 = ₹14,400$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days. Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for ₹ 7,200. With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to Kevin?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(6, 8, 3) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Arin}} = 4,\quad E_{\text{Selvi}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Total}} = 8$$
$$E_{\text{Kevin}} = 8 - (4 + 3) = 1$$
$$\text{Kevin's share} = \frac{1}{8} \times 7200 = ₹900$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Fifteen persons working 12 hours a day earn ₹18,000 per week. How many rupees will 18 persons working 9 hours a day earn per week?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: P and Q can do a work in 12 days and 9 days, respectively. They both worked together and earned ₹63,000. The share of P (in) is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } P : Q = \frac{1}{12} : \frac{1}{9} = 3 : 4$$
$$\text{Share of P} = \frac{3}{3 + 4} \times 63000 = \frac{3}{7} \times 63000 = 27,000$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A, B and C can do a work in 10 days, 15 days, and 20 days, respectively. They finished that work together and got ₹2,600 as wages. Find C's wage.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies: } A : B : C = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{15} : \frac{1}{20} = 6 : 4 : 3$$
$$\text{Sum of ratio} = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13$$
$$\text{C's wage} = \frac{3}{13} \times 2600 = ₹600$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: 4 women and 7 men earn a total of ₹ 11,480 in 7 days, while 10 women and 17 men earn a total of ₹ 36,360 in 9 days. How much will 11 women and 9 men together earn (in ₹) in 13 days?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Daily earning of } 4W + 7M = \frac{11480}{7} = 1640$$
$$\text{Daily earning of } 10W + 17M = \frac{36360}{9} = 4040$$
$$\text{Multiplying first equation by 5: } 20W + 35M = 8200$$
$$\text{Multiplying second equation by 2: } 20W + 34M = 8080$$
$$\text{Subtracting: } 1M = 120 \implies W = \frac{1640 - 7(120)}{4} = \frac{800}{4} = 200$$
$$\text{Daily earning of } 11W + 9M = 11(200) + 9(120) = 2200 + 1080 = 3280$$
$$\text{Earning in 13 days} = 3280 \times 13 = ₹42,640$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Ashok and Anil undertake to do a piece of work for ₹ 4,500. Ashok alone could do the work in the 8 days and Anil in 12 days. With the assistance of Amar, they finished the work in 4 days. What is the share of Amar?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 12, 4) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Ashok}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Anil}} = 2,\quad E_{\text{Combined}} = 6$$
$$E_{\text{Amar}} = 6 - (3 + 2) = 1$$
$$\text{Amar's share} = \frac{1}{6} \times 4500 = ₹750$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Anita and Anand can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They undertook to complete that work for ₹48,000. With the help of Arun, they completed the work in 6 days. Find the sum of the shares of Anita and Anand (in ₹).
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 18, 6) = 36\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Anita}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Anand}} = 2,\quad E_{\text{Combined}} = 6$$
$$\text{Combined share of Anita and Anand} = \frac{3 + 2}{6} \times 48000 = \frac{5}{6} \times 48000 = ₹40,000$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: X, Y and Z can do a piece of work in 4 days, 5 days and 7 days, respectively. They get ₹415 for completing the work. If X, Y and Z have worked together to complete the work, what is X's share?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } X : Y : Z = \frac{1}{4} : \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 35 : 28 : 20$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 35 + 28 + 20 = 83$$
$$\text{X's share} = \frac{35}{83} \times 415 = 35 \times 5 = ₹175$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Tina alone can do a piece of work in 12 days and Meena alone can do the same work in 15 days. If Tina and Meena undertook to do this work for ₹18,000, then how much amount will Meena get, if they work together?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Tina : Meena} = 15 : 12 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Meena's share} = \frac{4}{9} \times 18000 = ₹8,000$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Mohit and Rohit undertook a work for ₹4400. Mohit alone can do that work in 10 days and Rohit alone can do the same work in 15 days. If they work together, then what will be the difference in the amount they receive?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Mohit : Rohit} = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 3 + 2 = 5$$
$$\text{Difference in amount} = \frac{3 - 2}{5} \times 4400 = \frac{1}{5} \times 4400 = ₹880$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Rani can do a work in 10 days, Priya can do the same work in 15 days and Guddu can do the same work in 12 days. If they do that work together and they are paid ₹9000, then what is the share of Priya?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies Rani : Priya : Guddu} = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{15} : \frac{1}{12} = 6 : 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 6 + 4 + 5 = 15$$
$$\text{Priya's share} = \frac{4}{15} \times 9000 = 4 \times 600 = ₹2400$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn ₹ 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B ?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies: } A : B : C = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{20} : \frac{1}{30} = 6 : 3 : 2$$
$$\text{Total parts} = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11$$
$$\text{Parts of }(A + C) - B = (6 + 2) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5$$
$$\text{Difference in earnings} = \frac{5}{11} \times 1100 = ₹500$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A can complete a task in 12 days and B can complete the same task in 18 days. They start working together but A works for only 2 days. The remaining work is completed by B. If the total wage is ₹ 2,400, then what is B's share (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Work done by A in 2 days} = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}$$
$$\text{Work done by B} = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$$
$$\text{B's share} = \frac{5}{6} \times 2400 = 5 \times 400 = ₹2,000$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A, B and C can do a work in 8, 10 and 12 days, respectively. After completing the work together, they received ₹ 5,550. What is the share of B (in ₹) in the amount received?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 10, 12) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 15,\quad E_B = 12,\quad E_C = 10$$
$$\text{Total efficiency} = 15 + 12 + 10 = 37$$
$$\text{B's share} = \frac{12}{37} \times 5550 = 12 \times 150 = ₹1,800$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A and B worked together and received a total of ₹ 18,000 for 15 days. A's efficiency in the work was 5 times that of B's. The daily wage of A (in ₹) was:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Combined daily wage} = \frac{18000}{15} = 1200$$
$$E_A = 5 E_B \implies \text{Ratio } A : B = 5 : 1$$
$$\text{Daily wage of A} = \frac{5}{6} \times 1200 = ₹1,000$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: A can do a piece of work in 8 days while B alone can do it in 12 days. They work together for 4 days and the remaining work is completed by C alone in 2 days. They are paid ₹ 7,200 for the completion of the entire work. The earnings of A, B and C, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 12) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 3,\quad E_B = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 4 days} = 4 \times 3 = 12\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{12}{24} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 4 days} = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{8}{24} = \frac{1}{3}$$
$$\text{Work done by C in 2 days} = 24 - (12 + 8) = 4\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{4}{24} = \frac{1}{6}$$
$$\text{Earnings of A} = \frac{1}{2} \times 7200 = ₹3,600$$
$$\text{Earnings of B} = \frac{1}{3} \times 7200 = ₹2,400$$
$$\text{Earnings of C} = \frac{1}{6} \times 7200 = ₹1,200$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: WORK & WAGES
questions.questionText: Samir and Puneet can complete the same work in 10 days and 15 days respectively. The work was assigned for ₹ 4500. After working together for 3 days Samir and Puneet involved Ashok. The work was completed in total 5 days. What amount (in ₹) was paid to Ashok?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Samir}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Puneet}} = 2$$
$$\text{Samir and Puneet worked for all 5 days.}$$
$$\text{Work done by Samir in 5 days} = 5 \times 3 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by Puneet in 5 days} = 5 \times 2 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work completed by Ashok} = 30 - (15 + 10) = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Ashok's share} = \frac{5}{30} \times 4500 = \frac{1}{6} \times 4500 = ₹750$$
